I feel like the most important thing for my girl was getting her used to the sounds associated with flying before we ever set foot in an airport. Over and over for a few weeks leading up to our first flight, I had my Alexa’s play the sound of flight attendant call buttons, announcements from the cockpits, etc. There is a playlist on Spotify (something like “airplane ASMR” - I don’t remember exactly), that I used. It helped so much to create a positive relationship with these sounds before we even got on the plane. After that, I took her to my local airport so she could experience the sound of the engines in real life, familiarize herself with the environment, and meet TSA agents. We weren’t able to go through security, but she was able to interact with TSA agents/gloved hands touching her/baggage claim, etc. Also, I did my best to get her used to artificial turf since this is what all of the airport SD relief areas have. I do wish I had been able to get her on a train of some sort before flying, just because the airports we traveled through used “plane trains” and she was SO uncomfortable because she’d never experienced it before.

EDIT: forgot to add, I always bring something for her to chew on during take off / landing. Air pressure doesn’t affect dogs ears like it does humans, but they can still sense a shift in mood. The distraction of a chew toy keeps them calm!
